  PROBLEM: The first half of the test only checks the `captured_at` format with `re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z", ...)`, so it does not prove that `EPOCHREALTIME` takes precedence over the short fake `date +%3N` reading. The whole-seconds fallback also produces a matching `...:SS.000Z` value.
  WHY: If the EPOCHREALTIME branch in scripts/alert_inbox_capture.sh (lines 226-231 per z-ai_glm-5_3-flash) is removed or breaks, the test still passes and the #9240/#9405 regression guard goes undetected. There is no production impact. Every reviewer rated it NIT, mapped here to low. minimax_minimax-m3 raised it only as a hardening suggestion (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2). The suggested fix is to assert that `captured_at` is within a few seconds of a timestamp taken just before `_send`, or that it does not start with "2026-11-18T01:02:03".
- tests/test_alert_inbox_store.py:3-8 (module docstring) | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The module docstring contradicts itself. Line 5 says "one retry on HTTP 409" and lines 7-8 say "The 409 retry now repeats up to three times before the store fails".
  WHY: scripts/alert_inbox_store.sh (`409)` branch, `conflict_retried -lt 3`) and the tests test_third_conflict_is_still_retried / test_fourth_conflict_fails implement three retries. The stale clause misstates the retry contract but causes no runtime failure. Every reviewer rated it NIT, mapped here to low. The fix is to remove "one retry on HTTP 409," from line 5.

- tests/test_tg_helpers_alert_inbox.py:test_captured_at_ignores_a_short_date_reading, first half | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After `_send(env, "ERROR")` with the fake `date` that prints "2026-11-18T01:02:03.12Z" for any `%3N` format, the test only checks the `captured_at` format. If the EPOCHREALTIME branch were removed, the last fallback would call the real `date` and produce a valid `...:SS.000Z` value, so the test would still pass.
  WHY: Production behaviour is not affected, but the guard against the #9240 short-digit reading can be removed without any CI failure. Fix: assert that `captured_at` does not end in `.000Z`, or compare it to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (difference under 5 s). About 2 lines.
- tests/test_alert_inbox_store.py:lines 5-8 of the module docstring | severity=NIT | confidence=5

  WHY: There is no runtime failure, but the docstring misstates the retry contract. Fix: remove "one retry on HTTP 409," from line 5.

  SEVERITY: NIT | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
